html:
SMTO-LLM-0025 — The model service had a problem on its side

GUID: de4df3aa-5d02-4521-8218-48d71a28ebc9
Slug: provider-server-error
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • The model service reported an internal error while handling SMTO's request. SMTO doesn't know which part of the service failed, and nothing from this request was carried out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO runs the model for you, open the Inference page and check that the model instance is running. A model instance that has stopped or crashed causes errors like this.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This small test shows whether the service is handling requests again.
  3. When the check passes, on the stopped task, select Resume (or Continue task if that is what it shows). The failed request did nothing, so continuing is safe and earlier finished steps are kept.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model passes and the task continues without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages the model server. Include the time it happened so they can find it in their logs. Changing SMTO's settings won't fix a fault inside the service.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The provider or an intermediary returned an HTTP 5xx server error (provider_server_error), not attributed to memory exhaustion or model loading; the failed component is unknown.

What this means

  • An HTTP server-error status was returned by the provider or an intermediary. The status is evidence of a service-side failure response, not proof of GPU exhaustion or a particular failed component.

Why this can happen

  • The serving endpoint or intermediary returned a 5xx response.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact status and request time with provider and proxy health records. A proxy failure and a model-server failure may have different owners.

How to fix it

  • Use http_status and the request time to inspect provider and proxy logs; restore service health (for example a crashed worker, an upstream failure or a misconfigured gateway), verify with Check saved model or a small request to the endpoint, then resume. A 5xx alone is not evidence of GPU exhaustion.
  • Ask the provider operator to investigate the recorded status and service health before testing another model request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A controlled request returns a complete response without a server-error status.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Status classification describes this model request and grants no authority to replay earlier tools.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
